question: Should `promptly-prompt` be admitted to the ClawHub catalog, and as which package family, after reviewing its prompt-submission hook, provenance, and namespace?
rationale: The current source supports plugin publication, but accepting a third-party hook that changes prompt context is a product and trust-boundary decision that automation should not make.

options.title: Keep Open For Review
options.body: Maintain the issue while a human confirms package family, namespace/provenance, publication terms, and hook safety before any catalog listing.

options.title: Accept Through Package Publish
options.body: If the hook is acceptable, ask the upstream owner to publish through the supported ClawHub package flow with validation and source metadata instead of changing this repo directly.

options.title: Decline Catalog Admission
options.body: Close after maintainer review if prompt-intercepting hooks or the requested namespace are not acceptable for ClawHub publication.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Review
recommendation.body: Maintain the issue while a human confirms package family, namespace/provenance, publication terms, and hook safety before any catalog listing.

likelyOwner.reason: The current package catalog and validation contract history points to Patrick-Erichsen as the best available package-catalog routing owner.
